documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter check. Good overall. Breathing unchanged, climbs her stairs fine, slows on the hill behind the library. No exacerbations. Back: the usual ache after a long day, no sharp pain. Knees stiff in the morning, loosen after 10 minutes. Acetaminophen a few times a week.
Taking calcium twice a day with meals and vitamin D.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs with decreased air movement at bases, no wheeze. Heart regular. Kyphosis. Knees crepitant.

A/P
COPD stable. Osteoporosis on calcium/D. Knee OA.
RTC 6 months or AWV in the fall.

documents.title: Wellness check call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Outreach call to older patients with lung disease during the pandemic. Pt and husband staying home, son drops off groceries. No fever, cough or shortness of breath beyond baseline. Has enough of her supplements and acetaminophen. Knows to call for any respiratory symptoms. Offered video visit if needed.

events.reason: Severe low back pain after lifting

conditions.label: Acute osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture of T12

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe pain; #15, no refills

reports.text: Thoracic and lumbar spine, AP and lateral. Comparison 5/10/2019. Compression fracture of the T12 vertebral body with further loss of anterior height compared with the prior study. No retropulsed fragment. Other thoracic and lumbar vertebral heights preserved. Diffuse osteopenia. Thoracic kyphosis.
reports.conclusion: T12 compression fracture, progressed since 2019, consistent with a new acute osteoporotic fracture at the same level.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 7/24/2020.

CC: severe low back pain.

HPI: 74F, osteoporosis with a T12 compression fracture last year. This afternoon she picked up a heavy carton of canning jars and had immediate severe sharp pain in the middle of her low back. Does not travel down the legs. Denies trauma, fever, incontinence of bowel or bladder, or weight loss.

Meds: calcium, vitamin D, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.
Social: former smoker quit ~15 yrs, minimal alcohol, retired teacher.

Exam: vitals normal. Afebrile. Tender to palpation over T12. No neurological deficit; strength, sensation and reflexes normal. SLR negative both sides.

Labs: Ca 9.8, phos 3.5, alk phos 70, vitamin D 30. COVID PCR negative.
XR T and L spine: T12 compression fracture, more height loss than 2019.

Impression: acute osteoporotic T12 compression fracture, recurrent at the same level, neuro intact.

Plan: acetaminophen around the clock, tramadol prn (#15). Ice/heat. No lifting. Close PCP follow-up; consider outpatient options for her osteoporosis with PCP.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record received for Friday's visit: T12 fracture again. Called pt. Pain bad first two nights, a bit better now. Acetaminophen every 6 hours, tramadol at night. No numbness, weakness or incontinence. Prefers video visit this week rather than coming in; booked Thursday.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - Post-ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is at her kitchen table, husband helping with the tablet. Consent for video visit given.

ED 7/24: new T12 compression fracture after lifting a box of jars. ED record and films reviewed.

Pain 6/10, much like last time. Sleeping in the recliner. Acetaminophen every 6 h, tramadol once or twice a day. Constipated since the tramadol, prune juice helping. No leg numbness, weakness or incontinence.

Obs: comfortable seated, gets up slowly, walks across the kitchen without assistance.

A/P
Recurrent T12 osteoporotic compression fracture.
- Same plan as 2019: acetaminophen, tramadol only when needed, short.
- Stool softening with fluids and prunes.
- No lifting. Her son will help with the canning this year.
- Calcium and vitamin D continue.
Follow up in the office in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, masked in-person.

Interval: second T12 fracture in July, slowly settling.

Function: independent but doing less. Balance class closed since spring; she does the exercises at home from the handout. Misses seeing people, but talks to her daughters every day. PHQ-2 1, not depressed per her.
No falls.

Exam: vitals as charted. Kyphosis more pronounced. Mild T12 tenderness still. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

Prevention: flu this week at nurse visit. COVID vaccine when available. Mammogram due spring. Colonoscopy: last 2013 normal, turns 75 soon, we agreed no further screening.

RTC 3 to 4 weeks to recheck back.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary - Orthopedic Surgery
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, orthopedic surgery service. Admitted 9/7/2021, discharged 9/11/2021 to a skilled nursing facility for rehabilitation.

Diagnosis: displaced left femoral neck fracture.
Procedure: left total hip arthroplasty, 9/8/2021.

History: 75-year-old woman with osteoporosis and two prior T12 compression fractures (2019, 2020). At home on 9/7 she caught her foot on a rug and fell straight onto her left side. Immediate severe left hip pain, unable to stand. No head strike, no loss of consciousness.
PMH: osteoporosis, COPD, postmenopausal, pill esophagitis (2018).
Home meds: calcium carbonate, vitamin D3, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, minimal alcohol, retired teacher, lives with husband.

Exam on arrival: left leg shortened and externally rotated. Could not bear weight on the left. Distal pulses and sensation intact.
Imaging: left hip radiographs show a displaced femoral neck fracture, with the cortical outline broken and an irregular lucent fracture line. Chest X-ray clear.
Pre-op labs unremarkable.

Course: medically cleared. Left total hip arthroplasty on hospital day 2 without complication. Perioperative cefazolin. Mobilized with PT on POD 1, weight bearing as tolerated with posterior hip precautions. Pain controlled. Voiding, bowels moving.

Discharge meds: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily to complete 28 days (last dose 10/6); oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 q6h prn severe pain; acetaminophen 500 mg prn mild pain (count toward daily acetaminophen total); calcium carbonate; vitamin D3; multivitamin.
Follow-up: orthopedics wound check and X-ray at 6 weeks; PCP after discharge from rehab. Recommend outpatient bone health follow-up with PCP.

documents.title: Hospital notification
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Husband called: Ruth fell at home last week, broke her left hip, had a hip replacement and is at a rehab facility. Discharge summary received yesterday and routed to PCP. Will call when she is home to set up a transitional visit.

documents.title: Skilled Nursing Facility Discharge Summary
documents.author: skilled nursing facility
documents.body:
Short-term rehabilitation stay 9/11/2021 to 9/24/2021 after left total hip arthroplasty.

PT/OT: progressed from walker with standby assist to independent with a rolling walker for household distances; stairs with rail and supervision. Posterior hip precautions reviewed with patient and husband. Raised toilet seat and shower chair arranged.
Nursing: incision healing, staples removed 9/22, no drainage. Enoxaparin daily, self-injecting with teaching complete. Oxycodone-acetaminophen used about once a day the first week, none in the last 4 days.
No falls during stay.

Discharged home with home physical therapy 2 to 3 times weekly. Remaining enoxaparin through 10/6. PCP follow-up next week. Allergies NKDA.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM interactive contact, day after discharge home from rehab. Pt home with husband. Walker, managing stairs with rail. Home PT starts Wednesday. Injecting enoxaparin herself. Pain controlled with acetaminophen. Med list reviewed by phone. Visit tomorrow 2 pm.

conditions.label: Presence of left artificial hip joint

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Interactive contact by RN 9/27 (day after rehab discharge).

Fell 9/7 tripping on the hall rug, displaced L femoral neck fracture, L total hip 9/8, two weeks of rehab, home 9/24. Hospital and rehab summaries reviewed.

Today: walking with a rolling walker, husband drove her in. Home PT coming Mon/Thu. Pain 2 to 3/10, only acetaminophen now; has 12 oxycodone tablets left and doesn't want them. On enoxaparin, injecting herself, last dose 10/6. Eating less, lost a couple of pounds. Bowels ok. No calf pain, no chest pain or breathlessness beyond her usual.
The rug is gone.

Med reconciliation: enoxaparin 40 mg daily to 10/6; acetaminophen 500 mg prn; calcium carbonate 1250 mg bid; vitamin D3 1000 units; multivitamin. Oxycodone-acetaminophen: advised to bring to the drop box.

Exam: vitals as charted. Incision L lateral hip clean, dry, well healed, no erythema. L calf soft, nontender. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. S/p L THA for displaced femoral neck fracture. Doing well. Hip precautions. Ortho at 6 weeks.
2. Osteoporosis with 3 fragility fractures. Calcium and vitamin D. Fall prevention reviewed again.
3. Weight down, encourage protein, small frequent meals.
RTC 6 to 8 weeks, sooner prn.

documents.title: Home health certification
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Home health PT plan of care received for signature: gait and transfer training, hip precautions, strengthening, 2 to 3 visits a week for 4 weeks after left total hip arthroplasty. Face-to-face encounter 9/28. Signed and faxed back.

documents.title: Last shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Did my last enoxaparin shot yesterday! Where do I put the sharps container? Also my PT says I can go to a cane in the house. Is that ok with you?

documents.title: RE: Last shot
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Congratulations! You can drop the closed sharps container at the town transfer station's medical waste bin or bring it to us. Yes, follow your PT's lead on the cane. Keep the hip precautions until ortho clears you.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Hyperinflated lungs. Patchy opacity in the right lower lobe. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Degenerative changes and kyphosis of the thoracic spine with known T12 deformity.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe opacity consistent with pneumonia.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Acute Visit - Cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit. Four days of cough bringing up yellow-green phlegm, fevers at home to 101 last night, more winded than usual walking to the mailbox. Achy. No chest pain. No sick contacts she knows of, but she's been at PT and the grocery store. Home COVID test negative yesterday.

Hip recovery going fine, using a cane.

Exam: vitals as charted. Tired appearing, speaking in full sentences. Crackles at the right base, no wheeze. Heart regular. Calves soft.
CXR in office: RLL opacity.

A/P
Community-acquired pneumonia, RLL, in a 75-year-old with COPD. Not toxic; outpatient treatment reasonable.
- Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 bid x7 days plus azithromycin x5 days.
- Albuterol inhaler to have on hand for the shortness of breath; inhaler technique shown with a spacer.
- Fluids, rest. Call Friday with an update; ER for worse breathing, confusion or chest pain.

documents.title: Pneumonia check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called as asked. Fever gone since yesterday, cough looser, appetite coming back. Used albuterol twice, helped. Taking the antibiotics with food, some loose stool but not watery. Will finish course Monday. Advised to call if diarrhea worsens.

conditions.label: Severe Clostridioides difficile infection without toxic megacolon

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth four times daily for 10 days

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary - Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service. Admitted 11/19/2021, discharged home 11/23/2021.

Diagnosis: severe Clostridioides difficile infection, no toxic megacolon.

History: 75F, three days of watery diarrhea, crampy belly pain and low-grade fever. Hospitalized in September for a left hip fracture (total hip, then rehab). Has COPD and finished an oral antibiotic course for pneumonia about two and a half weeks ago.
Home meds: calcium carbonate, vitamin D3, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, minimal alcohol, retired teacher.
Family: mother osteoporotic hip fracture; father COPD; maternal grandmother ovarian cancer.

Admission vitals: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), BP 130/85, HR 92, RR 18.
Exam: mild LLQ tenderness without rebound or guarding; hyperactive bowel sounds; no peripheral edema; otherwise unremarkable. Healed L hip incision.
Labs: WBC 15,000, Hgb 13.2, platelets 250,000, creatinine 1.0, electrolytes normal. Stool C. difficile toxin positive (resulted 11/20).

Course: contact precautions, IV fluids, oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily from 11/19. Fever resolved by day 2, stools down to 2 to 3 a day and thickening by discharge. Tolerating diet. No abdominal distension; imaging not needed.

Discharge: complete oral vancomycin 125 mg QID for 10 days total (last dose 11/28). Avoid unnecessary antibiotics. Handwashing with soap and water, bleach cleaning of bathroom. PCP visit within 1 week.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after discharge yesterday. Diarrhea slowing, 3 soft stools today, no fever. Taking vancomycin four times a day, last dose Sunday. Husband bleaching the bathroom. Drinking well. Appt next Tuesday.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admitted 11/19 to 11/23 with severe C. diff after the pneumonia antibiotics. Discharge summary reviewed. RN call 11/24.

Finished oral vancomycin on Sunday. One or two soft stools a day now, formed this morning. No fever. Eating, but weight is down to 55 kg from about 58 last year. Tired. Cough from the pneumonia is gone, no albuterol use for two weeks.
Hip: walking with cane outdoors, none indoors. Ortho happy at 6 weeks.

Exam: vitals as charted. Thin, but looks better than I expected. Lungs clear, no crackles at R base. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds.

A/P
1. Severe C. difficile infection, completed vancomycin, improving. Watch for relapse; call for 3 or more loose stools a day. Antibiotics only if clearly needed.
2. Pneumonia, resolved clinically.
3. Weight loss after two hospital stays. Protein shakes between meals. Recheck weight in 6 weeks.
4. Hip arthroplasty, recovering well.
5. Osteoporosis on calcium and D.

documents.title: Follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Checked in after C. diff. Bowels normal, once a day, formed. No fever. Appetite good, drinking a shake every afternoon. Asked if she can get her flu shot now; yes, scheduled with nurse Thursday.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine was delayed this year by her hospital stays. High-dose flu IM L deltoid, Pfizer COVID booster IM R deltoid. Observed 15 minutes, fine.
